policy_extraction.implementation_notes: This is a request by the Irish SA to the EDPB for an Article 64(2) GDPR opinion on AI model data processing questions. It is not itself a binding decision or guidance document; it poses questions for EDPB harmonisation. Explicitly limited to GDPR/LED application only, excluding the AI Act, DMA, DGA, DSA interplay.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The document is centrally framed around data subjects' fundamental rights under GDPR. The IE SA's request focuses on ensuring lawful processing of personal data in AI model development, protecting data subjects across the EU/EEA from rights violations, and achieving harmonized enforcement of data protection law. The language consistently foregrounds data subject rights, legal bases for processing, and compliance obligations rather than economic competitiveness, security threats, or societal disruption.

evidence_spans.quote: The training and use of AI Models, including so-called 'large language models', gives rise to a number of wide-ranging data protection concerns. The issues arising impact data subjects across the EU/EEA.

just because personal data is made public does not mean that it is no longer personal data. Careful consideration of this situation is required in order to demonstrate compliance under data protection legislation
